A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MediRound work, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v2's Appendices A–F can be matched to material retained, revised, or omitted in v5, which has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation experiments, backbone and reference-input ablations, threshold sensitivity results, and dataset analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains original segmentation experiments and ablations and adds an evaluation by 15 medical students in Section 5.6 and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The specified JCM supervision changes: v2 Appendix A computes the quality target from the corrected mask, whereas v5 Section 4.4 and Figure 6 use an uncorrected mask decoded separately from the original feature. The core architecture remains unchanged. Algorithm 1's arbitrary prior-round reference clarifies behavior already described in v2.

E1.justification: MR-MedSeg and SA-Med2D-20M segmentation coverage is retained. v5 adds a human evaluation of educational utility involving medical students, introducing a new evaluation task and participant population. The educational reframing does not establish a change to the image datasets.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including human-assisted segmenters, MLLM–segmenter combinations, SegLLM-7B/13B, and MediRound+READ. Single-round comparators and backbone ablations also match. Newly cited MTurn-Seg and MedVL-SAM2 are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v5 introduces a human-study protocol with 15 medical students rating four criteria on a five-point scale. Existing segmentation splits, metrics, and stated training budgets remain unchanged. Added explanations of baseline training and historical-mask access document existing comparisons without establishing that their protocols changed.

E4.justification: v5 omits v2's category-frequency analysis and additional interactive cases in Appendices D–E, including Figures B–C. The threshold and backbone ablations remain, and the reference-input ablation moves unchanged from Appendix C/Table A to Section 5.4/Table 5. The main qualitative comparison is also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new student-rating chart provides aggregate scores without uncertainty; its participant count is an evaluation-design detail.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes SegLLM test metric assignments: for example, SegLLM-7B regular-case Dice/gIoU/cIoU changes from 42.4/42.1/32.9 to 42.1/32.9/42.4. MediRound scores and retained ablation results are unchanged. Figure 9 adds practicality/helpfulness/convenience/potential scores of 3.80/3.93/4.33/4.07. Appendix dataset statistics and additional qualitative results are omitted.

T1.justification: v5 Equation (4) explicitly distinguishes the uncorrected mask from the corrected prediction, and Section 4.4 revises the mathematical definition of the quality target accordingly. Other forward and loss formulations are retained or relocated. Neither version presents theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central task, 177K-dialogue dataset, MediRound/JCM contributions, and segmentation-performance claims remain. v5 elevates educational benefits to central abstract and introduction claims, emphasizing progressive learning by non-experts. v2 already briefly mentioned learning medical knowledge, but primarily motivated broader clinical interaction.

C2.justification: v5 removes all four explicit limitations from v2 Appendix F: one object per turn, sensitivity to long queries, near-loss of general conversational ability after specialization, and inability to process 3D images or videos. It also adds a semantic-drift rationale for JCM and interprets student ratings as evidence of educational value. These substantially change the stated applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v5 discloses Dice/BCE loss weights of 0.5/2.0, baseline fine-tuning versus zero-shot status, human prompting procedures, and historical-mask access. It recharacterizes 118K images and 569K masks as an initial candidate pool. Conversely, detailed scenario counts, modality names, reference-phrasing guidance, and the explicit release promise from v2's appendix disappear; the project link and core implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v5 adds MTurn-Seg as concurrent multi-turn medical segmentation work, cites MedVL-SAM2, and adds the GPT-5 system card. It also uses existing READ and MediSee references to motivate intervention at the SEG embedding. The broader relationship to LISA, SegLLM, and medical segmentation research remains.

P1.justification: The opening narrative is substantially rewritten around medical education. The method becomes four numbered subsections, training material from Appendices A–B enters Section 4.4, and Appendix C's ablation enters the main experiments. Other appendix sections disappear, ablation and qualitative sections exchange order, and a human-evaluation section is added.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column layout to a predominantly single-column format, substantially resizing and relocating displays. Figure 1 adopts learner imagery, the JCM training diagram is revised and moved into the main text, Table A becomes Table 5, appendix Table B and Figures B–D disappear, and Figure 9 adds the student-rating chart.

improvement.justification: v5 improves the consistency of JCM's documented quality supervision, clarifies evaluation and loss settings, and adds evidence about perceived educational utility. However, it removes detailed dataset analyses and concrete limitations, including conversational degradation that matters to its stronger educational framing. The small rating study does not resolve those concerns, so the substantive benefits and losses do not support a reliable net-quality judgment.
